newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian inflation drops to 2.2 percent in March.
newsitem.headline: Italian inflation drops to 2.2 percent in March.

text.p: Italian inflation fell to 2.2 percent year-on-year in March, less than half its level 12 months ago, national statistics institute ISTAT said on Monday.
The drop in the consumer price index (CPI) was exactly in line with expectations and kept inflation at its lowest levels since May 1969, the last time it stood at 2.0 percent.
The figure compared with 2.4 percent in February and 4.5 percent in March 1996. The month-on-month rise was unchanged at 0.1 percent.

Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi said at the weekend that Italian CPI would fall to 1.9 percent in April and could dip to 1.5 percent by June. The government has set a target of annual average inflation of 2.5 percent for 1997.
Inflation has not dropped below the psychological threshold of two percent since April 1969, when it was 1.9 percent.

The Bank of Italy has twice cut key interest rates in the past year, each time by 75 basis points, in response to falls in inflation. Traders said that if April inflation fell below 2.0 percent, the central bank could act again.
The official discount rate is now 6.75 percent.
